items.title: Caris Life Sciences launches Caris Detect — most comprehensive MCED blood test yet
items.summary: Caris Life Sciences commercially launched Caris Detect on July 1, a multi-cancer early detection (MCED) blood test using ultra-deep Whole Genome Sequencing, Whole Transcriptome Sequencing, and AI to detect cancer signals across multiple cancer types. The Achieve 1 study (3,014 subjects) reported 61.3% Stage I–II sensitivity and 99.2% specificity in asymptomatic individuals — among the highest published figures in the MCED field. Unlike competitors relying on methylation or cfDNA fragment analysis alone, Caris Detect combines DNA and RNA signals.
items.why: Caris Detect enters the MCED market directly competing with Galleri and Cancerguard; Protocol's SPOT-MAS positioning should be stress-tested against this new benchmark on sensitivity and technology breadth, and the market launch validates growing consumer/payer readiness for blood-based cancer screening.

items.title: US Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program goes live at $50/month — landmark access shift
items.summary: Starting July 1, the US Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) began covering select GLP-1 weight-loss medications (Wegovy, Zepbound KwikPen, Foundayo) at a $50 monthly copay for eligible Medicare beneficiaries. The pilot runs through December 2027 and applies to individuals with BMI ≥35, or BMI 27–35 with qualifying comorbidities. This is the first time the US government has covered obesity medications for Medicare's ~65 million enrollees.
items.why: The largest national payer in the world now subsidising GLP-1s for weight loss signals an irreversible mainstreaming of medical weight management — reinforcing demand for Protocol's GLP-1 program and setting a pricing reference point that Asian markets and private payers will watch closely.

items.title: Singapore HSA opens public consultation on mandatory health supplement notification
items.summary: Singapore's Health Sciences Authority (HSA) launched a 4-week public consultation (July 1–29) on a proposed Complementary Health Products regulatory framework that would make pre-market product notification mandatory for health supplements — replacing the current voluntary system active since 2022. If adopted, full compliance (including mandatory notification and labeling) would phase in from Q3 2028 to Q3 2030. The proposal also removes pre-publication advertising permit requirements in favour of post-market surveillance.
items.why: Protocol operates in the Singapore regulated health space; the incoming framework will raise compliance, labeling and traceability requirements for any supplements bundled with Protocol's screening or longevity protocols — worth monitoring and submitting feedback during the consultation window.

items.title: FDA public comment period closes on proposed ban of bulk-compounded GLP-1s
items.summary: The comment period for the FDA's April 30 proposal to remove semaglutide, tirzepatide, and liraglutide from the 503B outsourcing facility bulk drug substances list closed on June 29. If finalised — expected Q3 2026 — large-scale compounding pharmacies will be prohibited from producing GLP-1 injectables in bulk, ending the era of cheap compounded Ozempic/Wegovy alternatives that has driven much of the direct-to-consumer telehealth GLP-1 market.
items.why: A compounded GLP-1 ban raises effective market prices for weight-loss medications globally and strengthens the case for Protocol's branded, clinician-supervised GLP-1 program versus unregulated online compounders — a competitive positioning advantage worth communicating to patients.

items.title: GRAIL's Galleri MCED test: FDA PMA review ongoing, Medicare coverage set for 2028
items.summary: GRAIL submitted the final module of its Premarket Approval application for the Galleri multi-cancer early detection test to the FDA in January 2026, with the review ongoing. A complementary legislative milestone: the US Congress passed spending provisions establishing a Medicare coverage pathway for MCED tests from 2028. Galleri's PATHFINDER 2 trial data — showing >7-fold increase in cancer detection when added to standard screening — underpins the PMA. An FDA decision is widely anticipated in late 2026.
items.why: If Galleri receives FDA approval in H2 2026, it will become the first government-cleared MCED test, accelerating payer coverage and global adoption of the cancer blood test category — directly relevant to how Protocol positions and prices SPOT-MAS, and a signal to watch for regulatory timelines in Singapore/APAC.
